title: Cylinder
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to -90.0 degrees, 0.0 degrees, and -90.0 degrees, and a translation vector of [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]. On the first face, draw a 2D sketch consisting of a closed loop with four lines: the first line starts at (0.0, 0.0) and ends at (0.75, 0.0); the second line starts at (0.75, 0.0) and ends at (0.75, 0.011); the third line starts at (0.75, 0.011) and ends at (0.0, 0.011); and the fourth line starts at (0.0, 0.011) and ends at (0.0, 0.0). Scale the 2D sketch by a factor of 0.75. Rotate the scaled 2D sketch using the same Euler angles and translate it using the same translation vector. Extrude the 2D sketch 0.0257 units along the normal direction to create a new solid body. The resulting part is named the cylinder, which has a rectangular base with a length of 0.75 units, a width of 0.011 units, and a height of 0.0257 units. This part forms the foundation for the subsequent steps in creating the final cylindrical shape.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.011) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.011) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.0257)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# The Euler angles are (-90, 0, -90) and the translation vector is (0, 0, 0)
# This transformation is equivalent to rotating the object 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# The final model is represented as 'r'
